title: Gynaecological Oncology
curriculum: Super-Speciality (MCh / DrNB Gynaecological Oncology / Gynecologic Oncology)
examPattern: NEET-SS Gynaecological Oncology Specialty Group paper (150 MCQs spanning cervical preinvasive and invasive malignancies, endometrial cancer and molecular genomics [TCGA/ProMisE], epithelial and non-epithelial ovarian neoplasms, borderline tumors, vulvar and vaginal cancers, gestational trophoblastic disease, sentinel node algorithms, radical cytoreductive surgery, HIPEC, pelvic exenteration, systemic targeted/immunotherapies, and palliative oncology).

modules.name: Cervical Cancer Screening, HPV Virology & Prophylactic Vaccines

mustKnow.fact: High-risk HPV genotypes 16 and 18 account for approximately 70% of invasive cervical cancers globally, while HPV 16 is most carcinogenic and HPV 18 is disproportionately enriched in cervical adenocarcinomas.

HPV oncogenes E6 and E7 drive neoplastic transformation by targeted ubiquitin-mediated degradation of p53 tumor suppressor protein via E6AP and functional inactivation/degradation of retinoblastoma protein (pRb) respectively.

The nonavalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil 9) targets low-risk types 6 and 11 (causing 90% of genital warts) and high-risk types 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58, preventing up to 90% of HPV-attributable cervical cancers.

Primary HPV testing is recommended by WHO and ACS starting at age 25 years every 5 years as the preferred screening modality over cytology alone due to superior clinical sensitivity for high-grade CIN3+ lesions.
mustKnow.source: WHO Guidelines for Screening and Treatment of Cervical Pre-cancer Lesions

mustKnow.fact: In co-testing algorithms (cytology plus HPV testing), women aged 30 to 65 years with negative cytology and negative high-risk HPV have a 5-year risk of CIN3 below 0.1%, justifying a 5-year screening interval.

Dual-staining for p16INK4a and Ki-67 cellular biomarkers identifies simultaneous cell cycle arrest and aberrant proliferation, offering high specificity for detecting transforming high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.

In immunocompromised women, particularly those living with HIV, cervical cancer screening should initiate within 1 year of sexual debut or HIV diagnosis, utilizing primary HPV testing with re-screening every 3 years.
mustKnow.source: WHO 2021 Cervical Screening in Women Living with HIV

mustKnow.fact: Routine cervical cancer screening can be discontinued at age 65 in average-risk individuals with documented adequate negative prior screening (2 consecutive negative HPV tests or 3 negative cytology tests within 10 years, most recent within 5 years).

modules.name: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) & Colposcopy

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 8, DiSaia & Creasman 10e Ch 1

mustKnow.fact: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) is characterized by full-thickness architectural atypia and mitotic figures extending into the upper third of the cervical stratified squamous epithelium, serving as the definitive preinvasive cancer precursor.

ASCCP 2019 risk-based management thresholds dictate that immediate excisional treatment without mandatory preceding biopsy is expedited when the immediate risk of CIN3+ is 60% or greater (e.g., HPV 16 positive HSIL in post-reproductive patients).

Colposcopic evaluation requires visualization of the entire squamocolumnar junction (SCJ); a Type 3 transformation zone is situated entirely within the endocervical canal, rendering colposcopy unsatisfactory and necessitating endocervical curettage (ECC) or diagnostic excision.

High-grade colposcopic features predictive of CIN 2/3 include dense, opaque acetowhite epithelium with rapid uptake and slow fading, coarse punctation, coarse mosaicism, sharp bordered cuffed crypt openings, and atypical branching vessels.

Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP) and cold knife conization (CKC) are primary excisional therapies; CKC yields intact non-cauterized margins and is preferred when microinvasive carcinoma, adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), or high-grade endocervical disease is suspected.

For Adenocarcinoma in Situ (AIS), diagnostic conization with negative endocervical and ectocervical margins of at least 3 mm is mandatory; hysterectomy remains definitive therapy once childbearing is completed due to the frequent presence of skip lesions.

Cervical excisional procedures increase future pregnancy complications with an estimated 2-fold increased relative risk of preterm birth (<37 weeks) and cervical insufficiency, directly proportional to cone depth exceeding 10 to 15 mm.

Post-treatment surveillance following CIN2/CIN3 excision mandates HPV-based testing at 6 months, followed by annual HPV testing for 3 years, and continued long-term screening every 3 years for a minimum of 25 years due to persistent elevated cancer risk.

modules.name: Cervical Cancer FIGO 2018 Staging & Diagnostic Workup

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 9, FIGO Cancer Report 2018/2021

mustKnow.fact: The FIGO 2018 cervical cancer staging system allows the incorporation of modern cross-sectional imaging (MRI, CT, PET-CT) and surgical/pathological findings to assign clinical and pathological stage.

Stage IA represents microinvasive carcinoma diagnosed microscopically: IA1 has depth of stromal invasion <=3 mm, whereas IA2 has stromal invasion >3 mm and <=5 mm, with horizontal spread dimension removed from the 2018 definition.

Stage IB comprises invasive carcinoma confined to the cervix with depth of invasion >5 mm: IB1 is >=5 mm invasion and <2 cm largest dimension; IB2 is >=2 cm and <4 cm; and IB3 is >=4 cm largest dimension.

Stage II indicates tumor extending beyond the uterus: IIA involves upper two-thirds of vagina without parametrial invasion (IIA1 <4 cm, IIA2 >=4 cm); IIB exhibits parametrial invasion but not extending to pelvic sidewall.

Stage IIIC designates lymph node metastasis confirmed by imaging (r) or pathology (p): IIIC1 indicates pelvic lymph node involvement only, while IIIC2 indicates retroperitoneal para-aortic lymph node metastasis irrespective of tumor size.

Pelvic MRI is the imaging modality of choice for local tumor staging, delivering superior accuracy (>90%) for evaluating stromal invasion depth, cervical tumor size, parametrial infiltration, and vaginal fornix extension.
Whole-body 18F-FDG PET-CT has highest sensitivity (85-90%) and specificity (>95%) for detecting regional pelvic and distant retroperitoneal para-aortic nodal metastases in tumors >=IB2.

Stage IVA involves biopsy-proven mucosal invasion of the bladder or rectum with bullous edema alone insufficient; Stage IVB designates hematogenous or distant lymphatic dissemination beyond the para-aortic nodal basin.

modules.name: Early-Stage Cervical Cancer & Radical Hysterectomy

mustKnow.fact: Querleu-Morrow classification categorizes radical hysterectomy: Type A is minimal resection of paracervix; Type B is partial resection of uterosacral/vesicouterine ligaments with ureteral unroofing; Type C is complete resection of paracervix to pelvic sidewall and transection of uterosacral ligaments at rectum.

The prospective phase III LACC trial (Ramirez et al. 2018) demonstrated that minimally invasive radical hysterectomy (laparoscopic/robotic) was associated with statistically significant inferior disease-free survival (91.2% vs 97.1%) and higher overall mortality compared to open abdominal radical hysterectomy in early cervical cancer.

Sedlis criteria identify high-intermediate risk features after radical hysterectomy warranting adjuvant pelvic external beam radiation therapy: combinations of deep outer-third stromal invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), and large clinical tumor diameter (>=4 cm).

Peters criteria define high-risk pathology after radical hysterectomy requiring adjuvant concurrent cisplatin chemoradiotherapy: presence of positive pelvic lymph nodes, positive parametrial surgical margins, or positive mucosal resection margins.
mustKnow.source: Peters et al. J Clin Oncol 2000 (GOG 109)

mustKnow.fact: Nerve-sparing radical hysterectomy (Querleu-Morrow Type C1) preserves the hypogastric nerves (sympathetic), pelvic splanchnic nerves S2-S4 (parasympathetic), and inferior hypogastric plexus, dramatically reducing post-operative bladder denervation and urinary retention.

For Stage IA1 cervical squamous carcinoma without lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), simple extrafascial hysterectomy or therapeutic conization with negative margins achieves a cure rate exceeding 99% without lymphadenectomy.

In Stage IA1 with LVSI and Stage IA2, modified radical hysterectomy (Querleu-Morrow Type B) with systematic bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy or sentinel lymph node mapping is the standard oncologic management.

Ovarian preservation and transposition (oophoropexy) at least 2 to 3 cm above the pelvic brim outside the planned radiation field can be safely performed during radical surgery in premenopausal women with squamous histology <4 cm.

modules.name: Fertility-Sparing Surgery in Cervical Cancer (Trachelectomy)

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 10, NCCN Cervical Guidelines 2024

mustKnow.fact: Radical trachelectomy involves surgical resection of the cervix, upper 1 to 2 cm of vagina, and adjacent parametrium, with preservation of the uterine corpus, fundus, and bilateral adnexa in reproductive-aged women seeking future pregnancy.

Standard eligibility criteria for radical trachelectomy include stage IA1 with LVSI, IA2, or IB1 tumors, histological diameter <=2 cm, squamous or typical adenocarcinoma subtype, absence of deep endocervical canal extension, and negative pelvic lymph nodes.

Histopathological contraindications to fertility-sparing trachelectomy include neuroendocrine/small cell carcinoma, gastric-type adenocarcinoma, adenoma malignum, deep cervical stromal invasion, and tumor size exceeding 2 cm.

Intraoperative frozen section analysis of the upper endocervical resection margin is mandatory; a tumor-free margin of at least 8 to 10 mm from the internal os is required to ensure oncological safety while preserving uterine function.

The prospective SHAPE trial (Plante et al. 2024) demonstrated that simple hysterectomy or simple conization is oncologically safe with non-inferior 3-year pelvic recurrence rates compared to radical hysterectomy in low-risk cervical cancer (<=2 cm, <50% stromal invasion).

Prophylactic permanent cervical cerclage using non-absorbable Mersilene or polypropylene tape is placed around the lower uterine segment/isthmus at the time of trachelectomy to prevent subsequent mid-trimester spontaneous abortion and cervical incompetence.

Following radical trachelectomy, all subsequent viable pregnancies must be delivered strictly by planned elective cesarean section at 37 to 38 weeks gestation with preservation of the permanent cerclage tape.

Oncological safety of radical trachelectomy is comparable to radical hysterectomy in appropriately selected <=2 cm tumors, with recurrence rates of 3% to 5% and overall live birth rates exceeding 65% to 70% among achieved pregnancies.

modules.name: Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer (LACC): CCRT & Brachytherapy

mustKnow.fact: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) with weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) and external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) followed by intracavitary brachytherapy is the international standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer (stages IB3 to IVA).

The definitive radiation treatment course, comprising external beam radiation therapy (45 to 50.4 Gy) plus high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy, must be completed within an overall total treatment time of 7 to 8 weeks (<=56 days) to avoid accelerated tumor clonogen repopulation.

Image-guided adaptive brachytherapy (IGABT) utilizes MRI at the time of applicator insertion to delineate high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV), delivering an equivalent total biological dose (EQD2) of at least 85 to 90 Gy to HR-CTV D90.

In FIGO 2018 stage IIIC2 (documented metastatic para-aortic lymphadenopathy), the radiation portal must be systematically extended superiorly to cover the para-aortic nodal chain up to the renal vessels (extended-field radiation).

The phase III INTERLACE trial demonstrated that induction chemotherapy with 6 weekly cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel preceding standard CCRT significantly improved progression-free survival (73% vs 64%) and overall survival in locally advanced cervical cancer.

The KEYNOTE-A18 trial demonstrated that the addition of pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) to standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (stages IB3-IIA2 with node-positive, or IIIB-IVA).

Radiation tolerance dose constraints for critical normal pelvic organs at risk (OAR) specify maximum EQD2 D2cc limits of <=90 Gy for bladder, <=70 to 75 Gy for rectum, and <=75 Gy for sigmoid colon to avoid severe radiation cystitis, proctitis, or fistulae.

Post-treatment surveillance response assessment is performed with whole-body 18F-FDG PET-CT at 12 to 16 weeks post-radiotherapy, providing strong prognostic predictive value for durable long-term local and distant disease control.

modules.name: Endometrial Hyperplasia, EIN & Lynch Syndrome Genetics

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 12, Williams Obs 25e Ch 33

mustKnow.fact: Endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN) / atypical hyperplasia represents a monoclonal premalignant lesion with an architectural volume percent stroma <55% and carries a 40% to 45% concurrent risk of invasive adenocarcinoma on definitive hysterectomy.
mustKnow.source: Mutter et al. Cancer 2000, ACOG Practice Bulletin

mustKnow.fact: Definitive standard management of endometrial hyperplasia with atypia (EIN) in postmenopausal or non-fertility-seeking patients is total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TH-BSO), avoiding morcellation.

For reproductive-aged patients with EIN desiring fertility preservation, high-dose progestin therapy utilizing levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine device (LNG-IUD 52 mg) or oral megestrol acetate (160 mg daily) achieves regression rates of 80% to 90% at 6 to 9 months.

Endometrial surveillance during conservative medical therapy mandates repeat hysteroscopy and endometrial biopsy every 3 to 6 months until two consecutive negative specimens are documented before attempting conception.

Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer) is caused by germline mutations in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2, conferring a 40% to 60% cumulative lifetime risk of endometrial cancer, often presenting as the sentinel primary malignancy.
terms: MMR genes MLH1 MSH2 MSH6 PMS2

mustKnow.fact: Universal screening of all newly diagnosed endometrial carcinomas for Lynch syndrome by immunohistochemistry (IHC) for MMR proteins or microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is recommended by SGO and NCCN.

Loss of MLH1 and PMS2 expression on IHC requires reflex MLH1 promoter hypermethylation analysis to differentiate sporadic epigenetic silencing (90% of cases) from germline Lynch syndrome mutations (10%).

In confirmed Lynch syndrome mutation carriers, risk-reducing total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is recommended upon completion of childbearing, typically between ages 35 and 40 (or 40 to 45 for MSH6/PMS2 carriers).

modules.name: Endometrial Cancer FIGO 2023 Staging & Surgical Principles

topics.book: FIGO Cancer Report 2023, Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 13

mustKnow.fact: FIGO 2023 endometrial cancer staging integrates histological grade, substantial lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), and molecular classification directly into surgical anatomical stage assignment.

Stage IA in FIGO 2023 is subclassified into: IA1 (non-aggressive histological type confined to an endometrial polyp or endometrium), IA2 (non-aggressive type invading <50% of the myometrium with no/focal LVSI), and IA3 (low-grade endometrioid adenocarcinomas limited to uterus and ovary).

Stage IB comprises non-aggressive histological types with >=50% myometrial invasion without substantial LVSI; Stage IC incorporates aggressive histological types (serous, clear cell, carcinosarcoma, mesonephric) limited to endometrium or invading myometrium without extrauterine spread.
Stage II comprises cervical stroma invasion (IIA), substantial lymphovascular space invasion (IIB), or aggressive histology with any myometrial invasion (IIC).

Stage IIIC indicates retroperitoneal nodal metastasis: IIIC1 indicates pelvic lymph node involvement (IIIC1i micrometastasis, IIIC1ii macrometastasis), and IIIC2 indicates para-aortic lymph node involvement (IIIC2i micrometastasis, IIIC2ii macrometastasis).

Standard comprehensive surgical staging for endometrial cancer comprises total extrafascial hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, peritoneal cytology, and bilateral pelvic and para-aortic lymph node assessment via sentinel lymph node mapping.

Minimally invasive surgery (laparoscopic or robotic-assisted) is the definitive standard of care for endometrial cancer staging based on the LAP2 (GOG) and LACE trials, showing equivalent oncologic outcomes with reduced wound complications and shorter hospitalization.
mustKnow.source: Walker et al. J Clin Oncol 2012 (LAP2)

mustKnow.fact: Omental biopsy or infra-colic omentectomy is mandatory during staging for high-risk aggressive histologies (uterine serous carcinoma, carcinosarcoma, and clear cell carcinoma) due to a 15% to 20% rate of occult microscopic omental metastases.

modules.name: TCGA / ProMisE Molecular Classification of Endometrial Cancer

mustKnow.fact: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and ProMisE classification stratify endometrial cancer into four distinct molecular subgroups: POLE ultramutated, Mismatch Repair Deficient (MMRd / MSI-H), p53 abnormal (p53abn / copy-number high), and No Specific Molecular Profile (NSMP / copy-number low).
mustKnow.source: Kandoth et al. Nature 2013 (TCGA), Talhouk et al. Cancer 2015

mustKnow.fact: POLE ultramutated subgroup (7-10% of cases) is characterized by pathogenic exonuclease domain mutations in POLE (e.g., P286R, V411L), extremely high tumor mutation burden (>100 mut/Mb), and excellent prognosis with near-zero recurrence rates, justifying adjuvant de-escalation.

p53 abnormal (p53abn / copy-number high) subgroup (15% of cases) is defined by aberrant TP53 expression on IHC (complete null/absence or strong diffuse >80% missense positivity), carries the worst clinical prognosis, and requires aggressive platinum-based adjuvant therapy.

Mismatch repair deficient (MMRd) subgroup (25-30% of cases) exhibits loss of MMR proteins (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), intermediate prognosis, and remarkable therapeutic sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors (PD-1 inhibitors like dostarlimab and pembrolizumab).

No Specific Molecular Profile (NSMP) subgroup (50% of cases) has normal MMR, wild-type p53, and wild-type POLE; clinical prognosis is intermediate and strongly correlates with estrogen receptor (ER) status and traditional clinico-pathological risk factors.

In FIGO 2023 staging, molecular classification modifies stage: a stage I or II tumor with confirmed POLE mutation is downstaged to Stage IAm(POLE), reflecting its outstanding clinical outcome regardless of histological grade.
Conversely, in FIGO 2023 staging, any Stage I or II endometrioid endometrial cancer harboring p53 abnormal (p53abn) molecular profile with myometrial invasion is upstaged to Stage IICm(p53abn).

The PORTEC-4a prospective randomized trial is the first clinical trial to tailor adjuvant therapy (omission vs vaginal brachytherapy vs external beam radiotherapy) based entirely on integrated molecular risk profiles rather than traditional histology alone.
mustKnow.source: van den Heerik et al. Lancet Oncol 2020 (PORTEC-4a)

modules.name: High-Risk Endometrial Cancer: Adjuvant RT, Chemotherapy & Immunotherapy

mustKnow.fact: The landmark PORTEC-3 trial demonstrated that combined adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (concurrent cisplatin during EBRT followed by 4 cycles of carboplatin-paclitaxel) significantly improved 5-year failure-free survival (76% vs 69%) and overall survival in high-risk endometrial cancer compared to pelvic radiotherapy alone.
mustKnow.source: de Boer et al. Lancet Oncol 2018 (PORTEC-3)

mustKnow.fact: The GOG-258 trial comparing adjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus 6 cycles of chemotherapy alone in stage III/IVA endometrial cancer found similar overall survival, but chemoradiotherapy significantly reduced local pelvic and para-aortic nodal recurrences (11% vs 20%).

Vaginal brachytherapy (VBT) alone provides effective local vault control equivalent to pelvic external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) in high-intermediate risk endometrial cancer (PORTEC-2 trial) while producing significantly less gastrointestinal toxicity and preserving quality of life.

In the phase III RUBY trial, adding dostarlimab (anti-PD-1) to carboplatin and paclitaxel produced a dramatic 72% reduction in risk of progression or death (PFS HR 0.28) in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR/MSI-H) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

The phase III NRG-GY018 trial demonstrated that the addition of pembrolizumab to carboplatin and paclitaxel reduced the risk of progression or death by 70% in dMMR endometrial cancer (HR 0.30) and also provided significant benefit in pMMR patients (HR 0.54).

For mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) advanced endometrial cancer progressing after first-line platinum chemotherapy, the combination of pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib (multi-tyrosine kinase inhibitor) significantly improved PFS and OS over second-line chemotherapy in KEYNOTE-775.

In HER2-positive advanced or recurrent uterine serous carcinoma (overexpressing HER2 in approximately 30%), the addition of trastuzumab to carboplatin-paclitaxel significantly prolonged median progression-free survival from 8.0 to 12.6 months.
mustKnow.source: Fader et al. J Clin Oncol 2018

mustKnow.fact: Low-grade endometrioid endometrial carcinoma with hormone-receptor (ER/PR) positivity recurring with indolent metastatic disease responds to hormonal therapy with megestrol acetate alternating with tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors (letrozole), or fulvestrant, achieving response rates of 25% to 30%.

modules.name: Uterine Leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) & Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma (ESS)

mustKnow.fact: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) is the most common pure uterine sarcoma, characterized pathologically by the Bell/Stanford triad: cytological atypia, tumor cell necrosis (coagulative necrosis), and mitotic index >=10 mitoses per 10 high-power fields (HPFs).
mustKnow.source: Bell et al. Am J Surg Pathol 1994, Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 14

mustKnow.fact: FIGO staging for uterine sarcomas (leiomyosarcoma and endometrial stromal sarcoma) is distinct from endometrial cancer: Stage I is confined to uterus (IA <=5 cm, IB >5 cm largest dimension); Stage II extends to pelvis; Stage III extends to abdominal tissues; Stage IV invades bladder/rectum or distant organs.

Intraperitoneal uterine morcellation of an unexpected leiomyosarcoma significantly worsens prognosis, converting stage I disease to disseminated intraperitoneal dissemination and reducing 5-year overall survival from 73% to 46%.
mustKnow.source: FDA Safety Communication 2014, Park et al. Ann Oncol 2011

mustKnow.fact: Standard primary surgical therapy for uLMS is total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; routine systematic lymphadenectomy is not recommended because regional lymph node metastasis occurs in <3% to 5% of apparent uterus-confined cases.

Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma (LG-ESS) is driven by recurrent chromosomal translocations, most commonly t(7;17)(p15;q21) resulting in JAZF1-SUZ12 fusion, shows strong ER/PR positivity, and carries an indolent course with late recurrence.

High-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma (HG-ESS) is frequently characterized by t(10;17)(q22;p13) producing YWHAE-NUTM2 fusion, lacks ER/PR expression, runs an aggressive clinical course, and requires cytotoxic chemotherapy.

For advanced, metastatic, or recurrent uterine leiomyosarcoma, first-line cytotoxic systemic chemotherapy consists of gemcitabine plus docetaxel, or doxorubicin monotherapy, achieving objective response rates of 25% to 35%.
mustKnow.source: Hensley et al. J Clin Oncol 2008 (SARC005)

mustKnow.fact: In low-grade ESS, estrogen replacement therapy and tamoxifen are strictly contraindicated due to agonist tumor stimulation; maintenance hormonal therapy with megestrol acetate, medroxyprogesterone, or aromatase inhibitors provides effective disease control.

modules.name: Uterine Carcinosarcoma (MMMT) & Rare Uterine Malignancies

mustKnow.fact: Uterine carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Mullerian tumor, MMMT) is biologically and genetically a metaplastic carcinoma (epithelial dedifferentiation) rather than a true sarcoma, and is therefore staged and treated following epithelial endometrial cancer paradigms.

Pathologically, carcinosarcomas contain malignant epithelial elements (most commonly high-grade serous or endometrioid) and sarcomatous components that are either homologous (indigenous tissue such as leiomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma) or heterologous (chondrosarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma).
mustKnow.source: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours

mustKnow.fact: Nearly 90% of uterine carcinosarcomas harbor TP53 mutations, exhibiting diffuse p53 immunohistochemical overexpression or null phenotype, reflecting an underlying molecular kinship with copy-number high uterine serous carcinomas.

Surgical staging for carcinosarcoma mirrors high-risk endometrial cancer, requiring total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy, and omentectomy due to a 30% to 40% rate of occult extrauterine metastasis at diagnosis.

In the prospective phase III trial GOG-261, carboplatin plus paclitaxel was demonstrated to be non-inferior in overall survival and significantly less toxic than paclitaxel plus ifosfamide, establishing carboplatin-paclitaxel as the first-line systemic chemotherapy standard for uterine carcinosarcoma.
mustKnow.source: Powell et al. J Clin Oncol 2022 (GOG-261)

mustKnow.fact: Metastatic dissemination in carcinosarcoma is predominantly driven by the epithelial (carcinomatous) component, with pelvic and distant lymphatic and peritoneal deposits consisting purely of carcinoma in over 80% of metastatic lesions.

Uterine adenosarcoma is a distinct biphasic neoplasm characterized by benign epithelial glands surrounded by malignant sarcomatous stroma displaying periglandular cuffing; presence of sarcomatous overgrowth (>25% pure sarcoma) confers high recurrence and metastatic risk.

PEComa (perivascular epithelioid cell tumor) of the uterus is driven by loss of TSC1 or TSC2 (tuberous sclerosis complex) leading to hyperactivation of the mTOR signaling pathway, demonstrating responsiveness to mTOR inhibitors such as nab-sirolimus.
mustKnow.source: Wagner et al. J Clin Oncol 2021

sections.name: Epithelial Ovarian, Fallopian Tube & Primary Peritoneal Cancers

modules.name: Ovarian Cancer Etiology, BRCA1/2, STIC & Risk-Reducing Surgery

mustKnow.fact: Serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) located in the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube is the recognized precursor lesion for greater than 70% to 80% of high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas (HGSOC), driven by early TP53 mutation signatures.
mustKnow.source: Crum et al. J Clin Oncol 2007, Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 15

mustKnow.fact: Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variants confer lifetime ovarian cancer risks of 40% to 50% (BRCA1) and 15% to 25% (BRCA2), typically manifesting as high-grade serous histotype with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD).

Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is recommended between ages 35 and 40 (upon completion of childbearing) for BRCA1 carriers and ages 40 and 45 for BRCA2 carriers, reducing ovarian cancer risk by 80% to 90%.

Pathologic processing of RRSO specimens mandates the SEE-FIM protocol (Sectioning and Extensively Examining the Fimbriated End) with complete longitudinal sectioning of fimbriae and 2 mm interval transverse blocking of tube and ovaries to identify occult STIC or microscopic invasive carcinomas (found in 3% to 7%).
mustKnow.source: Medeiros et al. Am J Surg Pathol 2006

mustKnow.fact: Universal genetic testing for germline and somatic BRCA1/2 variants and tumor Homologous Recombination Deficiency (HRD) status is standard for all patients diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer regardless of age or family history.

Combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP) use exerts a potent chemopreventive effect, reducing epithelial ovarian cancer risk by approximately 20% for every 5 years of use, with persistent protective benefit lasting over 30 years after cessation.

Opportunistic bilateral salpingectomy with ovarian conservation performed at the time of benign gynecologic surgery or permanent sterilization reduces subsequent epithelial ovarian cancer risk by 40% to 50% in the general population.

Lynch syndrome confers a 10% to 12% lifetime risk of epithelial ovarian cancer, predominantly characterized by endometrioid and clear cell histological subtypes with presentation at an earlier median age (42-45 years).

modules.name: Adnexal Mass Evaluation, Biomarkers & Risk of Malignancy Indices

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 15, DiSaia & Creasman 10e Ch 11

mustKnow.fact: The Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI 1, Jacobs) calculates malignancy risk as RMI = U x M x CA-125, where U is ultrasound score (0, 1, or 3), M is menopausal status (1 if premenopausal, 3 if postmenopausal), and CA-125 is absolute serum level; a score >200 carries 85% sensitivity and 97% specificity for malignancy.
mustKnow.source: Jacobs et al. Br J Obstet Gynaecol 1990

mustKnow.fact: Human Epididymis Protein 4 (HE4) is a superior serum biomarker to CA-125 in premenopausal women because it is not elevated in benign gynecologic conditions like endometriosis, adenomyosis, or pelvic inflammatory disease.

The Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) combines serum CA-125 and HE4 with menopausal status to calculate predictive index scores, categorizing patients into low-risk and high-risk groups for epithelial ovarian cancer.

IOTA (International Ovarian Tumor Analysis) Simple Rules utilize 5 ultrasound features of benignity (B-features: unilocular, solid <7 mm, acoustic shadows, smooth multilocular <100 mm, no vascularity) and 5 of malignancy (M-features: irregular solid, ascites, >=4 papillary projections, irregular multilocular-solid >=100 mm, very strong flow) to classify adnexal masses with >90% sensitivity.
mustKnow.source: Timmerman et al. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol 2008

mustKnow.fact: The IOTA ADNEX model is a polychotomous prediction model that incorporates clinical and ultrasound parameters to calculate individual probabilities of benignity, borderline tumor, stage I cancer, stage II-IV cancer, or secondary metastatic ovarian malignancy.

O-RADS (Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System) ultrasound risk stratification assigns categories 1 through 5, where O-RADS 4 represents intermediate risk (10% to <50% malignancy) and O-RADS 5 represents high risk (>=50% malignancy) mandating gynecologic oncologist referral.

In postmenopausal women, an asymptomatic simple unilocular thin-walled ovarian cyst <5 cm in maximum diameter with normal serum CA-125 carries a malignancy risk below 1% and can be safely managed with conservative ultrasound surveillance.

Image-guided percutaneous or transvaginal fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of an intact, potentially resectable cystic adnexal mass is strictly contraindicated due to risk of cyst rupture, iatrogenic tumor upstaging (from Stage IA to IC1), and chemical peritonitis.

modules.name: Epithelial Ovarian Cancer FIGO 2014 Staging & Histopathology

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 15, FIGO Cancer Report 2018/2021

mustKnow.fact: FIGO 2014 epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancer staging is an operative surgical-pathological staging system incorporating histological subtype and modern surgical findings.
mustKnow.source: Prat et al. FIGO Ovarian Cancer Staging 2014

mustKnow.fact: Stage I is confined to ovaries or fallopian tubes: IA involves one ovary/tube with intact capsule, no tumor on surface, negative washings; IB involves both ovaries/tubes with intact capsules; IC exhibits intraoperative surgical capsule rupture (IC1), capsule ruptured before surgery or surface tumor (IC2), or malignant cells in ascites/peritoneal washings (IC3).

Stage II indicates pelvic extension below the pelvic brim: IIA involves extension or implants on uterus, fallopian tubes, or ovaries; IIB involves extension to other pelvic intraperitoneal tissues (bladder, rectum, sigmoid, pelvic sidewall).

Stage III involves retroperitoneal lymph nodes or microscopic/macroscopic peritoneal metastasis beyond the pelvis: IIIA1 involves retroperitoneal lymph nodes only (IIIA1i <=10 mm, IIIA1ii >10 mm); IIIA2 involves microscopic extrapelvic peritoneal metastasis with or without retroperitoneal nodes.
mustKnow.source: Prat et al. Int J Gynaecol Obstet 2014

mustKnow.fact: Stage IIIB designates macroscopic extrapelvic peritoneal metastases <=2 cm in largest dimension with or without retroperitoneal nodal metastasis; Stage IIIC designates macroscopic extrapelvic peritoneal metastases >2 cm, including tumor capsule extension to liver/spleen surface.

Stage IV indicates distant metastases: IVA is confirmed positive malignant pleural effusion on cytology; IVB is parenchymal liver or spleen metastases, or extra-abdominal lymph node metastases (including inguinal and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy).

Kurman and Shih Type I vs Type II dualistic paradigm stratifies epithelial ovarian cancer: Type I neoplasms (low-grade serous, low-grade endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous) develop stepwise from precursor lesions, are clinically indolent, and exhibit KRAS, BRAF, PTEN, or ARID1A mutations.
mustKnow.source: Kurman & Shih Am J Surg Pathol 2010

mustKnow.fact: Type II neoplasms (high-grade serous, carcinosarcoma, undifferentiated) arise de novo or from STIC, are aggressively metastatic at presentation, show near-universal TP53 mutations (>95%), and display pronounced chromosomal instability and BRCA/HRD pathway alterations.

modules.name: Primary Cytoreductive Surgery & Residual Disease Status (R0)

mustKnow.fact: The fundamental oncologic objective of primary cytoreductive (debulking) surgery in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer is complete cytoreduction with zero gross residual disease (R0 resection), which confers the single strongest independent predictor of prolonged progression-free and overall survival.

Residual disease status is rigorously categorized as: R0 (complete resection with no macroscopic residual disease), optimal cytoreduction (macroscopic residual <=1 cm in maximal diameter, R1), and suboptimal cytoreduction (residual disease >1 cm, R2).

Extensive upper abdominal surgical procedures (diaphragmatic peritonectomy or full-thickness resection, splenectomy, distal pancreatectomy, liver wedge/peritonectomy, and cholecystectomy) increase R0 complete cytoreduction rates from 40% to over 75% in expert surgical units.

The prospective LION trial (Harter et al. 2019) demonstrated that in patients with advanced ovarian cancer undergoing complete macroscopic resection (R0) and clinically/radiologically negative lymph nodes, systematic pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy provided no progression-free or overall survival benefit but significantly increased operative morbidity and 60-day mortality (3.1% vs 0.9%).
terms: omission of systematic lymphadenectomy in R0

mustKnow.fact: En bloc pelvic resection with modified posterior exenteration (radical oophorectomy with rectosigmoid resection and end-to-end colorectal anastomosis) achieves complete pelvic tumor clearance in advanced disease with extensive cul-de-sac obliteration.

Preoperative laparoscopy utilizing the Fagotti scoring system (evaluating peritoneal carcinomatosis, diaphragmatic disease, mesenteric retraction, omental cake, bowel infiltration, stomach infiltration, and liver surface metastases) predicts surgical resectability; a Fagotti score >=8 identifies a high probability of suboptimal debulking, directing patients toward neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
mustKnow.source: Fagotti et al. Ann Surg Oncol 2006

mustKnow.fact: Diaphragmatic resection requires careful intraoperative communication with anesthesia for lung recruitment maneuvers during pleural closure or chest tube placement to evacuate pneumothorax and prevent postoperative respiratory compromise.

Protective temporary loop ileostomy is indicated following ultra-low colorectal anastomosis (<5 to 6 cm from anal verge), in patients receiving high-dose preoperative corticosteroids, or following multiple concomitant bowel resections to minimize anastomotic leak catastrophe.

modules.name: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy, Interval Debulking & HIPEC

mustKnow.fact: Four landmark randomized prospective phase III trials (EORTC 55971, CHORUS, JCOG0602, and SCORPION) demonstrated that neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT, typically 3 cycles) followed by interval debulking surgery (IDS) achieves equivalent median overall survival compared to primary debulking surgery (PDS) in stage IIIC/IV ovarian cancer.
mustKnow.source: Vergote et al. NEJM 2010, Kehoe et al. Lancet 2015

mustKnow.fact: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by IDS is associated with significantly reduced perioperative morbidity, lower rates of high-grade surgical complications (14% vs 24%), fewer stoma formations, and dramatically lower 28-day postoperative mortality compared to upfront PDS in high-tumor burden patients.

The Chemotherapy Response Score (CRS, Bohm et al.) evaluates histopathologic response in omental tissue after NACT on a 3-tier scale: CRS 1 (minimal or no response), CRS 2 (partial response), and CRS 3 (complete or near-complete pathological response with <=2 mm viable tumor foci), where CRS 3 strongly predicts superior progression-free and overall survival.
mustKnow.source: Bohm et al. J Clin Oncol 2015

mustKnow.fact: In the landmark Dutch phase III trial (OVHIPEC-1, van Driel et al. 2018), adding hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC with cisplatin 100 mg/m2 at 40 to 41 deg C for 90 minutes) at the time of interval debulking surgery significantly prolonged median recurrence-free survival (14.2 vs 10.7 months) and median overall survival (45.7 vs 33.9 months) without increasing postoperative complications.

Long-term 10-year follow-up data from OVHIPEC-1 confirmed a durable 10-month overall survival advantage (median OS 44.9 vs 34.9 months; HR 0.70) in the HIPEC group among patients achieving complete or optimal interval debulking surgery.

Nephroprotection during cisplatin-based HIPEC is vital: intravenous sodium thiosulfate administration (9 g/m2 bolus followed by 12 g/m2 infusion over 6 hours) is co-administered to neutralize circulating free platinum and prevent acute tubular necrosis.

Current NCCN guidelines recommend consideration of HIPEC with cisplatin (100 mg/m2) specifically at the time of interval debulking surgery for stage III disease following 3 cycles of NACT in patients achieving R0 or <=1 cm optimal resection.

Interval debulking surgery is typically planned after 3 to 4 cycles of platinum-taxane chemotherapy; continuing NACT beyond 4 cycles prior to surgery provides no additional surgical debulking benefit and induces cumulative bone marrow suppression and chemoresistant clone selection.

modules.name: Systemic Therapy: Platinum-Taxane, Bevacizumab & PARP Inhibitors

mustKnow.fact: Standard first-line adjuvant systemic chemotherapy for advanced epithelial ovarian cancer comprises 6 cycles of intravenous carboplatin (AUC 5 to 6) and paclitaxel (175 mg/m2 administered over 3 hours) delivered every 3 weeks.

In the GOG-218 and ICON7 phase III trials, adding bevacizumab (anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, 15 mg/kg or 7.5 mg/kg) concurrently with carboplatin-paclitaxel and continued as maintenance for 12 to 15 months significantly prolonged progression-free survival, with overall survival benefit in poor-prognosis suboptimally debulked patients.
mustKnow.source: Burger et al. NEJM 2011, Perren et al. NEJM 2011

mustKnow.fact: The SOLO-1 phase III trial demonstrated that maintenance olaparib (oral PARP inhibitor 300 mg twice daily for 2 years) in newly diagnosed BRCA1/2-mutated advanced ovarian cancer in clinical complete response achieved an unprecedented median PFS of 56.0 months versus 13.8 months (HR 0.33), with 67% surviving at 7 years.
mustKnow.source: Moore et al. NEJM 2018, DiSilvestro et al. J Clin Oncol 2023

mustKnow.fact: In the PRIMA trial, maintenance niraparib (individualized starting dose 200 mg or 300 mg daily based on baseline body weight <77 kg or platelets <150k/uL) significantly improved progression-free survival in homologous recombination deficient (HRD-positive) advanced ovarian cancer (median PFS 21.9 vs 10.4 months; HR 0.43).

The PAOLA-1 trial established that the combination of maintenance olaparib plus bevacizumab provided dramatic synergistic PFS and OS benefits specifically in patients with HRD-positive tumors (including both BRCA-mutated and BRCA-wild-type HRD), achieving a median OS of 75.2 months versus 57.3 months (HR 0.60).
mustKnow.source: Ray-Coquard et al. NEJM 2019, Ray-Coquard et al. Ann Oncol 2023

mustKnow.fact: Calvert formula calculates absolute carboplatin carboplatin dose in milligrams as Dose = Target AUC x (GFR + 25), with GFR capped at a maximum of 125 mL/min (maximum dose 750 mg for AUC 6) to avoid severe myelosuppression.
mustKnow.source: Calvert et al. J Clin Oncol 1989

mustKnow.fact: PARP inhibitor class-specific adverse events include early hematologic toxicities (anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia), mild gastrointestinal disturbance, transient serum creatinine elevation via inhibition of renal transporters MATE1/OCT2, and a 1.5% to 2% long-term risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia (MDS/AML).

Intraperitoneal (IP) chemotherapy (paclitaxel/cisplatin regimen per GOG-172) improves overall survival by 16 months over IV chemotherapy in optimally debulked (<1 cm) stage III ovarian cancer, but carries high catheter-related complication rates and neuro-nephrotoxicity.

modules.name: Malignant Ovarian Germ Cell Tumors: Dysgerminoma & Yolk Sac

mustKnow.fact: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant ovarian germ cell tumor (30-40%), characteristically presenting in adolescents and young women (median age 15-20 years), with bilateral ovarian involvement in 10% to 15% of cases.

Serum tumor markers for dysgerminoma include elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP), with low-level beta-hCG elevation in approximately 5% due to syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells; AFP is strictly normal.

Yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor) is the second most common MOGCT, characterized pathologically by pathognomonic Schiller-Duval bodies (glomeruloid structures with central fibrovascular core) and striking serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) secretion.

Fertility-sparing surgery (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, peritoneal washings, omental biopsy, and pelvic/para-aortic lymph node assessment with uterine and contralateral ovarian preservation) is standard for all stages of MOGCT desiring future childbearing.

Biopsy or wedge resection of a normal-appearing contralateral ovary in MOGCT is strictly contraindicated because it causes future peritubal adhesion formation and ovarian reserve depletion without oncologic benefit.

Stage IA pure dysgerminoma with negative surgical staging has a cure rate exceeding 95% with surgery alone, allowing safe omission of adjuvant chemotherapy and observation with serial tumor markers and imaging.
All yolk sac tumors regardless of stage require adjuvant platinum-based combination chemotherapy due to intrinsic high malignancy and early microscopic hematogenous and lymphatic dissemination.

In phenotypic females presenting with dysgerminoma or gonadoblastoma associated with pelvic pain or primary amenorrhea, karyotype testing is mandatory to rule out 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer syndrome), which requires bilateral gonadectomy due to a 30% risk of bilateral malignancy.

modules.name: Immature Teratoma, Embryonal Carcinoma & BEP Chemotherapy

mustKnow.fact: Immature teratoma (IT) is graded histopathologically using the Norris / Gonzalez-Crussi 3-tier grading system based on the quantitative amount of immature neuroectodermal rosettes and tubules per low-power field (Grade 1: <1 LPF, Grade 2: 1-3 LPFs, Grade 3: >=4 LPFs).

Stage IA, Grade 1 immature teratoma in children and young women is successfully managed with fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy alone without adjuvant chemotherapy, achieving a 5-year survival >95%.

Embryonal carcinoma of the ovary is an aggressive primitive germ cell malignancy occurring in children and young women (median age 14 years), characteristically producing both serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG), often causing precocious puberty or menstrual irregularity.

Standard first-line adjuvant systemic chemotherapy for malignant ovarian germ cell tumors is the BEP regimen: Bleomycin (30 units IV weekly, total cumulative dose capped at <=270 to 300 units), Etoposide (100 mg/m2 IV days 1-5), and Cisplatin (20 mg/m2 IV days 1-5) repeated every 3 weeks for 3 to 4 cycles.

Growing teratoma syndrome (GTS) is defined by paradoxical enlargement of metastatic retroperitoneal or peritoneal masses during or following chemotherapy for MOGCT in the presence of completely normalized serum tumor markers (AFP and hCG).

Pathologically, growing teratoma syndrome represents chemical retroconversion or selective elimination of malignant germ cells leaving purely benign mature teratomatous elements, and definitive management is complete surgical resection without further chemotherapy.

Pulmonary function testing (PFT) with diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) must be monitored before each cycle of bleomycin; a fall in DLCO below 70% of baseline or development of basal crackles mandates immediate and permanent bleomycin discontinuation.

Long-term reproductive and gonadal outcomes following fertility-sparing surgery and 3 to 4 cycles of BEP chemotherapy are excellent, with over 85% to 90% of surviving patients resuming normal regular menses within 6 to 12 months, without increased risk of congenital fetal anomalies.
mustKnow.source: Gershenson et al. J Clin Oncol 2007

modules.name: Granulosa Cell Tumors: Adult vs Juvenile & Inhibin / FOXL2

mustKnow.fact: Adult granulosa cell tumors (AGCT) represent 95% of ovarian sex cord-stromal malignancies, occurring typically in perimenopausal or postmenopausal women (median age 50-55 years), characterized pathologically by Call-Exner bodies (follicle-like rosettes) and nuclear grooves ('coffee bean' appearance).

Over 97% of adult granulosa cell tumors harbor the pathognomonic somatic missense mutation in the transcription factor gene FOXL2 (c.402C>G; p.C134W), serving as a definitive diagnostic molecular biomarker.

Granulosa cell tumors actively produce 17-beta-estradiol, causing peripheral hyperestrogenism that leads to abnormal uterine bleeding, postmenopausal bleeding, endometrial hyperplasia (25-50%), and concurrent well-differentiated endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma in 5% to 10% of patients.

Preoperative or intraoperative endometrial biopsy or curettage is mandatory in all patients undergoing conservative fertility-sparing surgery for AGCT to rule out concurrent endometrial hyperplasia or adenocarcinoma.

Inhibin B is the most sensitive and specific circulating serum tumor marker for monitoring granulosa cell tumors, rising months before clinical or radiological evidence of disease recurrence; serum anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) and Inhibin A serve as complementary biomarkers.

Juvenile granulosa cell tumors (JGCT) represent 5% of cases, occurring predominantly in children and young women <30 years, lacking FOXL2 mutations, driven by AKT1 mutations (often linked to Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome), and presenting with isosexual precocious puberty.

Adult granulosa cell tumors exhibit a distinct clinical hallmark of late indolent recurrence, with over 50% of recurrences manifesting >5 to 10 years after primary diagnosis (and up to 30 years), necessitating lifelong continuous clinical surveillance.
Systematic pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy can be safely omitted in clinically stage I granulosa cell tumors because regional lymph node metastasis occurs in <1% to 2% of encapsulated disease.

modules.name: Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumors, Gynandroblastoma & DICER1 Mutations

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 18, WHO Female Genital Tumours 5e

mustKnow.fact: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors (SLCT / androblastomas) are rare sex cord-stromal neoplasms (0.5%) occurring in young women (median age 25 years), characterized clinically by progressive virilization (hirsutism, temporal balding, voice deepening, clitoromegaly) in 30% to 50% of patients.

Pathognomonic somatic hotspot RNase IIIb domain mutations in DICER1 (e.g., E1705, D1709, G1809, D1810) occur in >60% of moderately and poorly differentiated Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors, disrupting microRNA biogenesis.

Germline DICER1 mutations predispose to the DICER1 pleiotropic familial tumor syndrome, characterized by familial ovarian SLCT, pleuropulmonary blastoma, cystic nephroma, multinodular goiter, and pituitary blastoma.
mustKnow.source: Schultz et al. J Clin Oncol 2014

mustKnow.fact: Serum testosterone is significantly elevated (>200 ng/dL or 7 nmol/L) in virilizing SLCT, while DHEA-sulfate (DHEAS) is characteristically normal, differentiating an ovarian stromal source from an adrenal cortical tumor.

Meyer histopathologic classification stratifies SLCT into well-differentiated (benign behavior), moderately differentiated, and poorly differentiated, with the presence of heterologous elements (gastrointestinal glands, rhabdomyosarcoma, cartilage) or retiform architecture indicating aggressive metastatic potential.
mustKnow.source: Prat et al. Semin Diagn Pathol 2005

mustKnow.fact: Well-differentiated stage IA SLCT is cured by unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy alone; conversely, poorly differentiated tumors, tumors with heterologous elements, or stage II-IV disease require adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy (BEP).

Gynandroblastoma is an exceedingly rare sex cord-stromal neoplasm characterized histologically by the definite and unequivocal coexistence of both female (granulosa cell) and male (Sertoli-Leydig cell) tumor components within the same mass.
mustKnow.source: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours

mustKnow.fact: Steroid (lipid) cell tumors, not otherwise specified (NOS), are virilizing tumors composed entirely of lipid-rich cells; malignant behavior is strongly predicted by tumor diameter >7 cm, >=2 to 3 mitoses per 10 HPFs, necrosis, and grade 2-3 cytological atypia.
mustKnow.source: Hayes & Scully Am J Surg Pathol 1987

modules.name: Borderline Ovarian Tumors (LMP) & Fertility Preservation

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 15, DiSaia & Creasman 10e Ch 11

mustKnow.fact: Borderline ovarian tumors (tumors of low malignant potential, LMP) are characterized pathologically by epithelial proliferation, stratification, nuclear atypia, and mitotic activity in the complete absence of destructive stromal invasion.

Microinvasion in serous borderline tumors is defined by single cells or small nests of epithelial cells invading stroma with no individual focus exceeding 5 mm or 10 mm2 in area, which does not alter the excellent 5-year survival (>98%).
mustKnow.source: Bell et al. Am J Surg Pathol 2004

mustKnow.fact: Peritoneal implants associated with serous borderline tumors are categorized into non-invasive implants (epithelial or desmoplastic) and invasive implants (destructive stromal infiltration); the presence of invasive implants is reclassified in the WHO 2020 system as low-grade serous carcinoma.
mustKnow.source: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours 5th Edition

mustKnow.fact: Molecular pathogenesis is distinct from high-grade serous cancer: over 70% of serous borderline tumors harbor activating KRAS or BRAF (V600E) mutations, with universal absence of TP53 mutations.
mustKnow.source: Singer et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2003

mustKnow.fact: Fertility-sparing surgery (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy or ovarian cystectomy) is oncologically safe in reproductive-aged women with stage I borderline tumors; cystectomy carries a higher local ovarian recurrence rate (12-15% vs 5%), but recurrences remain borderline and can be successfully re-excised with near 100% overall survival.

Full surgical staging for borderline ovarian tumors comprises peritoneal washings, multiple peritoneal biopsies, and infracolic omentectomy; routine systematic lymphadenectomy is strictly not recommended because nodal metastases do not impact overall survival.

Mucinous borderline tumors of intestinal type are frequently unilateral and very large; discovery of bilateral disease, ovarian surface involvement, or pseudomyxoma peritonei mandates appendectomy and upper GI endoscopy to exclude appendiceal or gastrointestinal primary metastasis.

Adjuvant systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy provide no survival benefit in completely resected borderline ovarian tumors with non-invasive implants, and should be strictly avoided due to potential toxic harm.

modules.name: Krukenberg Tumors & Metastatic Neoplasms to the Ovary

mustKnow.fact: Classic Krukenberg tumor is defined strictly by the World Health Organization as a metastatic ovarian neoplasm characterized pathologically by mucin-producing signet-ring cells within a cellular, sarcomatoid-like ovarian pseudostroma.
mustKnow.source: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours

mustKnow.fact: The primary site of origin in Krukenberg tumors is the stomach (gastric adenocarcinoma, diffuse / linitis plastica type) in 70% to 75% of cases, followed by colorectal (15%), breast (lobular carcinoma), and appendix.

Bilateral ovarian involvement is present in over 80% of Krukenberg tumors, characteristically presenting as solid, lobulated, asymmetrical ovarian masses with an intact, smooth external capsule without surface adhesions.
mustKnow.source: Kiyokawa et al. Am J Surg Pathol 2006

mustKnow.fact: Immunohistochemical profiling differentiates primary ovarian mucinous adenocarcinoma from metastatic colorectal/gastric adenocarcinoma: primary ovarian mucinous tumors are characteristically CK7 positive, CK20 negative or patchy, and PAX8 positive; while metastatic lower GI tumors are CK7 negative, CK20 diffuse positive, and CDX2 positive.
terms: CK7 negative CK20 positive CDX2 positive (colorectal)
mustKnow.source: Park et al. Am J Surg Pathol 2002

mustKnow.fact: Mucin special stains highlight the intracellular mucin displacement of the nucleus: signet-ring cells demonstrate intense positivity with periodic acid-Schiff with diastase (PAS-D), mucicarmine, and Alcian blue at pH 2.5.

The proposed route of metastatic dissemination to the ovaries in Krukenberg tumors is predominantly retrograde lymphatic permeation via the thoracic duct and retroperitoneal lymph nodes, explaining the frequent absence of diffuse peritoneal carcinomatosis.
mustKnow.source: Al-Agha & Nicastri Arch Pathol Lab Med 2006

mustKnow.fact: Metastatic breast carcinoma to the ovary is most frequently derived from infiltrating lobular carcinoma (due to loss of E-cadherin expression) rather than invasive ductal carcinoma, frequently infiltrating as linear single-file 'Indian file' chords.

Palliative cytoreductive metastectomy (bilateral oophorectomy) in solitary or oligometastatic ovarian metastases from gastric or colorectal primary may prolong median overall survival (from 9 months to 19-24 months) only when R0 complete macroscopic resection of all extra-ovarian disease is achieved.
mustKnow.source: Briasoulis et al. J Clin Oncol 2020

sections.name: Vulvar, Vaginal Cancers & Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia

modules.name: Vulvar Cancer FIGO 2021 Staging, SLNB & Radical Vulvectomy

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 20, FIGO Cancer Report 2021

mustKnow.fact: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma develops via two distinct etiopathogenic pathways: an HPV-associated pathway (30-40%, driven by HPV 16, preceded by high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion / uVIN, p16 diffuse positive), and an HPV-independent pathway (60-70%, driven by TP53 mutations, preceded by differentiated VIN / dVIN and lichen sclerosus).

Depth of stromal invasion is measured from the epithelial-stromal junction of the adjacent most superficial dermal papilla to the deepest point of tumor invasion; Stage IA is defined strictly as a solitary lesion <=2 cm with stromal invasion <=1.0 mm, which has a nodal metastasis risk <1%, allowing safe omission of lymphadenectomy.

In FIGO 2021 staging, nodal involvement is categorized into Stage III based on size and number: IIIA involves 1 or 2 lymph node metastases (<5 mm, IIIAi) or 1 metastasis >=5 mm (IIIAii); IIIB involves >=3 lymph node metastases <5 mm (IIIBi) or >=2 metastases >=5 mm (IIIBii); IIIC involves extracapsular nodal spread.

Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) utilizing technetium-99m (99mTc) radiocolloid and blue dye or near-infrared indocyanine green (ICG) is standard for unifocal primary tumors <4 cm with clinically negative groins (GROINSS-V studies), reducing groin wound breakdown and lymphedema from 40% to <10%.
mustKnow.source: van der Zee et al. J Clin Oncol 2008 (GROINSS-V I)

mustKnow.fact: Pathologic ultrastaging of sentinel lymph nodes with serial sectioning at 50 to 100 um intervals and cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) immunohistochemistry is mandatory to detect isolated tumor cells (ITCs <=0.2 mm) and micrometastases (>0.2 to <=2 mm).

The GROINSS-V II trial established that for patients with sentinel node micrometastases (<=2 mm), inguinofemoral radiotherapy (50 Gy) is a safe and effective alternative to complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy, achieving a low groin recurrence rate of 1.6% with reduced lymphedema.
mustKnow.source: Oonk et al. J Clin Oncol 2021 (GROINSS-V II)

mustKnow.fact: Separate-incision radical local excision (triple incision technique: one vulvar excision plus bilateral separate groin incisions) significantly reduces wound breakdown and infection rates compared to en bloc radical vulvectomy (butterfly incision) without compromising local control.
mustKnow.source: Byron et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1965, Hacker et al. 1981

mustKnow.fact: A microscopic tumor-free surgical resection margin of at least 8 mm on fixed histological processing (equivalent to 10 to 15 mm macroscopic surgical clearance in vivo) is required to minimize local vulvar recurrence.

modules.name: Extramammary Paget Disease, Vulvar Melanoma & Rare Vulvar Tumors

mustKnow.fact: Extramammary Paget disease (EMPD) of the vulva presents as an erythematous, eczematoid, pruritic plaque with white crusting ('strawberries and cream' appearance), characterized histopathologically by large intraepithelial Paget cells with abundant pale vacuolated mucin-rich cytoplasm.

Immunohistochemical staining profile for primary cutaneous EMPD is CK7 positive, CEA positive, EMA positive, and GATA3/GCDFP-15 positive, with CK20 negative and p63 negative; positivity for CK20 and CDX2 indicates secondary EMPD from underlying colorectal/anal adenocarcinoma.
terms: secondary EMPD CK20 positive CDX2 positive

mustKnow.fact: Primary EMPD is associated with an underlying invasive adenocarcinoma in approximately 10% to 15% of cases and an internal malignancy (urothelial, anorectal, breast) in 20% to 30%, mandating comprehensive screening with mammography, colonoscopy, and cystoscopy.

Surgical wide local excision for EMPD is plagued by high local recurrence rates (30-40%) due to extensive subclinical intraepithelial skip lesions extending far beyond visible gross margins; non-surgical alternatives for recurrent disease include topical imiquimod 5% cream and photodynamic therapy.
mustKnow.source: van der Linden et al. Lancet Oncol 2019

mustKnow.fact: Vulvar melanoma is the second most common vulvar malignancy (5%), arising predominantly on the clitoris or labia minora in postmenopausal women, staging microstaging depth using Breslow depth of invasion rather than anatomical FIGO staging.

Breslow thickness determines surgical radial margins for vulvar melanoma: in situ melanoma requires 0.5 to 1.0 cm margins; <=1.0 mm thickness requires 1.0 cm margins; 1.01 to 2.0 mm requires 1.0 to 2.0 cm margins; and >2.0 mm thickness requires 2.0 cm margins.

Molecular alterations in mucosal vulvar melanoma differ significantly from cutaneous melanoma, exhibiting a high frequency of activating KIT mutations (15-25%, notably exons 11 and 13) and NRAS mutations, but low BRAF V600E mutations (<10%), rendering KIT inhibitors (imatinib) clinically active.
mustKnow.source: Curtin et al. J Clin Oncol 2006

mustKnow.fact: Bartholin gland carcinoma is rare (1-2% of vulvar cancers) and staged by the classic Honan criteria: tumor replacing Bartholin gland, histopathology compatible with gland elements (adenocarcinoma or adenoid cystic), and absence of primary elsewhere; adenoid cystic variant is perineural-invasive and MYB-NFIB fusion-driven.

modules.name: Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia (VaIN) & Primary Vaginal Cancer

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 21, DiSaia & Creasman 10e Ch 9

mustKnow.fact: Primary vaginal cancer is an extremely rare malignancy (1-2% of gynecologic cancers); by FIGO diagnostic consensus, a neoplasm involving both cervix and vagina is classified as cervical cancer, while a neoplasm involving both vulva and vagina is classified as vulvar cancer.

Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (VaIN 3) is strongly linked to high-risk HPV (HPV 16 in >70%), frequently occurring at the vaginal vault apex in patients who have undergone prior hysterectomy for CIN 3 or cervical cancer.

Treatment modalities for high-grade VaIN include topical imiquimod 5% cream, topical 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), CO2 laser ablation (requiring >=1 mm vaporization depth to destroy occult crypts), or surgical upper vaginectomy if invasive cancer cannot be excluded.

FIGO clinical staging of vaginal cancer: Stage I is limited to vaginal wall; Stage II involves subvaginal tissue invasion without extension to pelvic sidewall; Stage III extends to pelvic sidewall; Stage IVA invades bladder/rectal mucosa or direct extension beyond true pelvis; Stage IVB designates distant metastases.
terms: Stage I limited to vaginal wall

mustKnow.fact: Definitive radiotherapy combining external beam radiation therapy (EBRT, 45-50 Gy) with interstitial or intracavitary brachytherapy (total cumulative EQD2 75 to 80 Gy to tumor volume) is the primary curative treatment for stages II through IVA vaginal carcinoma.

The lymphatic drainage of the vagina mirrors its embryologic origin: the upper two-thirds drains primarily into the pelvic internal and external iliac lymph nodes, whereas the lower one-third drains directly into the superficial and deep inguinofemoral lymph nodes.

Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix in young women is etiologically linked to in utero transplacental exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES) prescribed before 1971, typically arising on the anterior wall of the upper third of the vagina within areas of vaginal adenosis.

Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of the vagina (sarcoma botryoides) presents in infant girls (<2 to 3 years old) as polypoid, grape-like gelatinous masses protruding from the introitus, characterized pathologically by a subepithelial cellular 'cambium layer' of rhabdomyoblasts and desmin/myogenin IHC positivity.

modules.name: Hydatidiform Mole: Complete vs Partial Mole & Post-Molar hCG Surveillance

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 22, Williams Obs 25e Ch 20

mustKnow.fact: A complete hydatidiform mole is diploid (46,XX in 90%, 46,XY in 10%) and purely androgenetic in origin, arising from fertilization of an anucleate 'empty' ovum by a single haploid sperm that duplicates (monospermic) or two sperms (dispermic), with no maternal nuclear DNA.

A partial hydatidiform mole is triploid (69,XXY in 70%, 69,XXX, 69,XYY) and diandric, resulting from fertilization of a normal haploid ovum (23,X) by two sperms or a diploid sperm, containing one maternal and two paternal haploid chromosome sets with identifiable fetal/embryonic tissue.

Immunohistochemical staining for p57KIP2 (a maternally expressed, paternally imprinted gene product) definitively differentiates complete from partial mole: complete moles are p57-negative in cytotrophoblast and villous stroma (due to absence of maternal genome), whereas partial moles are p57-positive.

Suction curettage with the largest available cannula (10-12 mm) under real-time ultrasound guidance is the definitive evacuation method of choice for hydatidiform mole; medical induction with prostaglandins and oxytocin before evacuation is avoided due to the risk of uterine hyperstimulation and trophoblastic embolization.
The risk of developing post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) is 15% to 20% following a complete mole, but only 1% to 5% following a partial mole.

Post-evacuation serum quantitative beta-hCG surveillance mandates weekly measurements until levels become undetectable (<5 mIU/mL) for 3 consecutive weeks, followed by monthly measurements for 6 months for complete moles (and 1 month of normal value for partial moles).

Reliable contraception (oral contraceptive pills, barrier, or depot medroxyprogesterone) is strictly mandatory throughout the surveillance period to prevent pregnancy from confounding hCG interpretation; intrauterine device (IUD) insertion is contraindicated until hCG normalizes due to uterine perforation and infection risks.

Recurrent hydatidiform moles are rare (1-2%), and familial recurrent biparental hydatidiform mole is caused by homozygous autosomal recessive mutations in NLRP7 (75%) or KHDC3L, resulting in maternal epigenetic imprint establishment failure.

modules.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia: FIGO/WHO Prognostic Scoring & Choriocarcinoma

topics.book: Berek & Hacker 7e Ch 22, FIGO Cancer Report 2021

mustKnow.fact: FIGO 2000 criteria for the definitive diagnosis of post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN): a plateau in serum hCG (<=10% change) across 4 measurements over 3 weeks; a rise in hCG (>10%) across 3 measurements over 2 weeks; histologic diagnosis of choriocarcinoma; or persistent hCG detection >=6 months post-evacuation.

The modified FIGO/WHO prognostic scoring system stratifies patients into low-risk GTN (score 0 to 6) and high-risk GTN (score >=7) based on 8 prognostic factors: age, antecedent pregnancy, interval from index pregnancy, pre-treatment hCG, largest tumor size, site of metastases, number of metastases, and previous failed chemotherapy.

In the FIGO scoring system, brain and liver metastases receive the maximum risk score of 4 points, while lung metastases score 0 points and spleen/kidney score 1 point; antecedent term pregnancy scores 2 points, while previous mole scores 0 points.

Low-risk GTN (score 0-6) is treated with single-agent chemotherapy: methotrexate (MTX, 8-day regimen 1 mg/kg days 1,3,5,7 with folinic acid / leucovorin rescue 0.1 mg/kg days 2,4,6,8) or intramuscular actinomycin D (dactinomycin 1.25 mg/m2 every 2 weeks), achieving cure rates approaching 100%.

High-risk GTN (score >=7) mandates multi-agent systemic chemotherapy with the EMA-CO regimen: Etoposide, Methotrexate, Actinomycin D on days 1-2 alternating weekly with Cyclophosphamide and Oncovin (vincristine) on day 8, yielding cure rates of 85% to 90%.
mustKnow.source: Newlands et al. J Clin Oncol 1991

mustKnow.fact: Chemotherapy for GTN must be continued beyond the first normal serum hCG level: consolidation therapy comprises 2 to 3 additional cycles of chemotherapy past the first undetectable hCG value in low-risk GTN, and 3 to 4 consolidation cycles in high-risk GTN to prevent relapse.

Gestational choriocarcinoma is a pure epithelial malignancy composed of biphasic proliferation of syncytiotrophoblasts and cytotrophoblasts with extensive central hemorrhage and coagulative necrosis, characteristically lacking chorionic villi.
mustKnow.source: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumours

mustKnow.fact: Patients with high-risk GTN and brain metastases (FIGO Stage IV) require immediate whole-brain external beam radiation (30 Gy in 10 fractions) or intrathecal methotrexate (12.5 mg) combined with modified EMA-CO (infusional methotrexate dose escalated to 1 g/m2) to overcome the blood-brain barrier.
mustKnow.source: Newlands et al. Br J Cancer 2002

modules.name: Placental Site Trophoblastic Tumor (PSTT) & Epithelioid Trophoblastic Tumor (ETT)

mustKnow.fact: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) originates from neoplastic transformation of extravillous intermediate trophoblast of the placental bed, characterized pathologically by sheets of monomorphic intermediate trophoblasts infiltrating deeply between myometrial smooth muscle bundles.

Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT) is an exceedingly rare variant arising from chorionic-type intermediate trophoblast, characterized by nodular 'geographic' islands of monomorphic epithelioid cells surrounded by dense, extensive hyaline matrix mimicking squamous cell carcinoma.
mustKnow.source: Shih & Kurman Am J Surg Pathol 1998

mustKnow.fact: Circulating serum beta-hCG levels in PSTT and ETT are disproportionately low relative to massive clinical tumor burden (<1000 mIU/mL), but serum human placental lactogen (hPL) is strongly positive in PSTT and serves as a diagnostic immunohistochemical and serum marker.

Immunohistochemical signature differentiates PSTT and ETT: PSTT shows diffuse, strong positivity for hPL, CD146 (Mel-CAM), and HLA-G with focal p63; conversely, ETT displays diffuse, strong positivity for p63 and GATA3 with focal hPL.
terms: PSTT hPL positive CD146 positive HLA-G positive
ETT p63 diffuse positive GATA3 positive
mustKnow.source: Shih & Kurman Int J Gynecol Pathol 2001

mustKnow.fact: Unlike gestational choriocarcinoma, PSTT and ETT are intrinsically resistant to single-agent and standard EMA-CO chemotherapy regimens, making total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy the primary curative modality for disease confined to the uterus.

The strongest independent clinical predictor of mortality in PSTT and ETT is an interval >=48 months (4 years) between the antecedent antecedent pregnancy and disease diagnosis, which carries a dismal survival rate (<30%).
mustKnow.source: Schmid et al. J Clin Oncol 2009

mustKnow.fact: Pelvic and retroperitoneal lymphadenectomy is indicated during primary hysterectomy for PSTT and ETT because regional nodal metastasis occurs in 10% to 15% of surgical cases, in sharp contrast to other GTN subtypes where lymphadenectomy is omitted.

For metastatic or recurrent PSTT/ETT, platinum/etoposide-based regimens such as EP-EMA (etoposide, cisplatin alternating with etoposide, methotrexate, dactinomycin) or paclitaxel/cisplatin (TP/TE), or immunotherapy with PD-1 inhibitors (pembrolizumab, due to universal PD-L1 expression) offer salvage therapeutic responses.
